properties.abstract: The highest point of this hike through the Sparenmoos moorland up to the Hundsrügg offers fantastic panoramic views of 427 mountain peaks. Depending on the season, there are different discoveries to make along the way: in spring, there is a sea of apple blossom; in summer, contented Simmental cattle; and in autumn, the edible mushrooms that sprout up from the ground in this area.
properties.description:
This popular panoramic hike sets off from the car park at Berghaus Sparenmoos. Passing through Alpine meadows that are part of the “Federal inventory of moorlands of particular beauty and national importance”, the hiking trail heads gently uphill with the Hundsrügg in constant view.

In the Alpine spring, when the marshes are brimming with orchids, there is a high chance of spotting black grouse. In the Alpine summer, the many Simmental cattle go to show that mountain farmers made the Alpine cultural landscape of Nüjeberg what it is. From Läuber to Hürli, the narrow trail runs along the mountain slopes. The view up to the Stockhorn, Gantrisch and Ochse demonstrates the curvature of the Simmental valley beautifully. Don’t forget to look down at the ground beneath your feet too: the entire trail is a haven for boletus and chanterelle mushrooms. 

Hürli then brings us to the cherry on the cake of the panoramic trail. From the last cabin (which sometimes offers catering) by the side of the trail onwards, another peak becomes visible with each step you take. With the Wildstrubel in view to your left and the Gastlosen mountain range to your right, the trail winds its way uphill to the Hundsrügg. This section of the route can easily reveal new details in the panorama, flora and geology every day. If visibility is good, you can even see over the Euschelspass into the Jura mountains in this area. You can see Mont Blanc, the Eiger and, furthest on your left, even the Matterhorn in the distance. The Hundsrügg and the Matterhorn are geologically related. Both were pushed northwards by the African plate during the formation of the Alps. The geological Prealps, of which the Hundsrügg is part, are full of flowers. The Hundsrügg is the perfect place to take a break with its panoramic views of 427 peaks.

The route then leads southwest to the Erbetlaubgrat ridge. Legend has it the people of the Simmental valley, Saanen and Jaun held wild mountain parties here in celebration after the end of the Plague. Nowadays, the little Erbetlaubseeli lake is a popular subject for photographers. After descending to the Luegle crossing, the trail branches off to the left followed by a couple of patches of woodland. From the Schiltenegg onwards, the trail descends gently to where you set off at Berghaus Sparenmoos. Along the way, you will pass by a few Alpine cabins where Berner Alpkäse AOP cheese is made.
properties.title: Hundsrügg-Panoramaweg
